verdicts.summary: The roster read at release start swallows every failure and returns no tasks. Only the writes are retried, so a failed read leaves the stale roster and the thread stays Waiting until a restart.
verdicts.scenario: 1. A Claude session is released by idle, detach or runtime_error. 2. releaseEntry calls readReleasedBackgroundTasks (ProviderSessionManager.ts:1066). 3. projectionStore.getThreadRecords fails, for example because one provider-thread row fails to decode or the DB is busy. 4. Effect.catchCause at :483-488 logs a warning and returns []. 5. writeReleaseRecords gets releasedBackgroundTasks=[]; retryReleaseRecords (:919-953) retries with that same empty list. 6. The roster is never cleared and nothing retries the read. The thread stays Waiting, which is the bug this change fixes. It is a failure path only and the cause is logged.
verdicts.consequence: On a transient or decode failure of the read, the thread stays Waiting until startup recovery. Only a warning is logged. The write path retries and the read path does not.

verdicts.summary: The compare-and-set follows the same commitThenPublish shape as its siblings. The only hazard I found is the decode-to-encode round-trip mismatch, which finding 0 already states.
For Claude and Muse, attachedThreadIds plus the detached thread covers every thread that could hold a roster, because both runtimes are single-thread and release when the last thread detaches.
verdicts.scenario: I tried to leave a roster-holding thread out of the set in three ways. (a) The thread detaches earlier from a live session. A single-thread runtime releases on that detach, with detachedThreadId passed. (b) The attach-rollback helper empties attachedThreadIds without a release. It only removes a thread that was newly attached by the failed attach, because an already-attached thread returns early. (c) Rotating or re-attaching. A live session already holds its thread in attachedThreadIds.

verdicts.summary: Each clear event goes through the provider-thread.updated projection, which also rewrites the app thread's activeProviderThreadId and updatedAt. If a cleared provider thread is not the thread's active one, the active pointer would flip to it.
verdicts.scenario: 1. Release finds a provider thread with a matching providerSessionId and a non-empty roster. 2. writeReleasedBackgroundWorkEvents emits provider-thread.updated for it (ProviderSessionManager.ts:518-535). 3. ProjectionStore.ts:2249-2277 sets the app thread's activeProviderThreadId to event.payload.id and its updatedAt to now. If the thread has an older provider thread with the same providerSessionId and a leftover roster, clearing it makes that older one active. getThreadRecords also returns provider threads matched through owner_node_id or subagents (ProjectionStore.ts:3076-3092), not just those with thread_id equal to the thread. I did not establish whether such a provider thread can exist for Claude or Muse.
verdicts.consequence: Possible wrong activeProviderThreadId on release, and a bumped thread updatedAt. This would happen only if more than one provider thread can share one providerSessionId with a roster.
